question: A team lead worries that linking Google Drive will let Claude read everything the company keeps in Drive. What is the accurate and policy-appropriate response?
options: A) Claude works within the permissions the person already holds, and administrators can restrict it further.
B) Claude reaches only files created after the connection was made, so older company material is never included.
C) Claude gains access to the whole of Drive once linked, so the connection has to be re-approved every week.
D) Claude's access is decided entirely by the project it is used in, independently of the person's own account.
correct_answers: A) Claude works within the permissions the person already holds, and administrators can restrict it further.
explanations: Correct. Access follows the user's existing permissions in the source system, and Team and Enterprise administrators can narrow what connections may do; narrowing never grants more than the source system allows.
There is no rule that limits a connection to newly created files.
Connecting does not grant access beyond what the person can already open, and weekly re-approval is not how the control works.
The project does not override the account's permissions in the connected service.
